items.title: Make the rename-aware diff reader parse NUL-delimited output and fail loudly on unparseable rows
items.context: core/evidence-freshness.ts changedFilesBetween / changedFilesBetweenRenameAware / changedFileStatusesBetweenRenameAware. RED fixtures: a rename of a path with a space, a non-ASCII path, and a path containing a quote character, each asserting BOTH sides survive; an unparseable row raises instead of being skipped. Keep the throw on an unresolvable ref and document it as the contract; audit callers for any catch-and-return-empty.
items.userSees: Running `node packages/main/dist/tasks/single-owner-extraction-smoke.js` prints one line per reader case and ends `single-owner-extraction-smoke: PASS`. In a fixture repository where a file whose name contains a non-ASCII character is renamed, the reader reports both the old and the new path; a deliberately corrupted diff row makes the reader raise an error naming the row instead of returning a shorter list.

happy.desc: A rename of a path containing a space, a non-ASCII character, or a quote character yields both the old and the new path from changedFileStatusesBetweenRenameAware and changedFilesBetweenRenameAware.

verification.selector: [PASS] rename of a path with a quote reports both sides through both reader functions

happy.desc: materialHash and storyFilesHash computed with the new reader are byte-identical to the old reader over a fixture repository containing no quoted paths.

verification.selector: [PASS] plain-path repository: materialHash and storyFilesHash are byte-identical to the reference formulas

edge.desc: A deleted path remains reported, and a copy reports both sides, under NUL-delimited parsing.

verification.selector: [PASS] a copy record (C100) reports both sides through all three readers

edge.desc: An unresolvable ref still throws, and a fixture asserts that no caller in packages/main/src catches that throw and returns an empty array.

verification.selector: [PASS] no reader body catches, and no caller wraps these readers in catch { return [] }

adversarial.desc: An unparseable diff row raises an error naming the row rather than being skipped; a fixture that injects a malformed row asserts the raise.

verification.selector: [PASS] a malformed record makes every reader throw an Error naming the raw record instead of skipping it

verificationEvidence.note: Smoke cases for space, non-ASCII and quote renames each assert both sides come back from changedFilesBetweenRenameAware and changedFileStatusesBetweenRenameAware; the quote case selector is the strictest of the three printed lines.

items.title: Delegate the DONE-required command parser to the canonical legacy parser and prove all call sites agree
items.context: core/done-required-validation.ts private SHELL_META_RE / splitShellWords / commandFromString around lines 40, 113, 276 versus parseLegacyValidationCommandString in core/validation-command-identity.ts. RED fixture: a shared set of tricky inputs (metacharacters, quoted arguments, embedded spaces) parsed through every call site must agree on shell-versus-argv; any intentional divergence becomes an explicit, named, tested difference.
items.userSees: The smoke prints one line per parser case and ends `single-owner-extraction-smoke: PASS`; `grep -n splitShellWords packages/main/src/core/done-required-validation.ts` prints nothing, and a DONE-required command containing a quoted argument with an embedded space executes exactly as it did before the change.

happy.desc: done-required-validation.ts delegates its command-string parse to parseLegacyValidationCommandString and no private SHELL_META_RE, splitShellWords or commandFromString remains in it.

verification.selector: [PASS] structural: done-required-validation.ts defines no private parser and imports the canonical one

edge.desc: A committed corpus of tricky inputs (metacharacters, quoted arguments, embedded spaces, empty string) produces identical shell-versus-argv results through every call site.

verification.selector: [PASS] corpus: the canonical parser produces the pinned {shell, command, args} for every entry

adversarial.desc: If the DONE-required path needs any divergence from the routine parse, it is an explicit named function with its own fixture; a fixture asserts no unnamed divergence exists by diffing outputs over the corpus.

verification.selector: [PASS] corpus: the DONE-required executor path and handlers/verifier.ts produce the same {shell, command, args} for every entry

verificationEvidence.note: Structural case reads done-required-validation.ts and fails while SHELL_META_RE, splitShellWords or commandFromString exist or the canonical import is missing.

items.title: Extract one story-workspace resolver with the phase-terminal guard and migrate the four existing resolver implementations onto it
items.context: story-query.ts readStoryProjection, session.ts listActiveWorktrees and readStoryFromLinkedWorktree, local-assurance-story-projection.ts collectLinkedStoryWorktrees, validation-plan.ts resolveStoryWorkspace. The helper returns gitCwd via resolveGitCwd, a workspace-rooted StoryStore and workspace-loaded config, and applies the phase-terminal guard (`phase !== 'DONE' && phase !== 'DISCARDED'`). RED fixture per migrated site: invoke from a different cwd and assert identical output, modelled on B-a745's F-010 main-checkout and wrapper-root cases; plus a DONE-story case asserting the guard refuses a merged-and-removed worktree.
items.userSees: The smoke prints one line per resolver case and ends `single-owner-extraction-smoke: PASS`. `node packages/main/dist/cli.js validation_plan --storyId=<active story> --tier=fast --json` run from the story worktree and from the main checkout prints the same selectionDigest, and run against a DONE story it reports the story as not resolvable from a linked worktree rather than reading a removed worktree.

happy.desc: One helper in core/story-workspace.ts returns gitCwd via resolveGitCwd, a workspace-rooted StoryStore and workspace-loaded config, and the four named implementations call it instead of their own logic.

verification.selector: [PASS] structural: the four implementations delegate to resolveStoryWorkspace and their own resolution logic is removed

edge.desc: The phase-terminal guard is an explicit option whose default matches each migrated caller's prior behaviour, and a fixture per migrated caller asserts DONE-story reads behave exactly as before.

verification.selector: [PASS] guard: a DONE story with a residual worktree is refused under the guard (rootReason=terminal-phase) and read from the residue only when the option is off

edge.desc: For each migrated caller, invoking from the story worktree and from the main checkout yields identical output, and a configured wrapper-root layout resolves the story worktree.

verification.selector: [PASS] validation_plan: the report (selectionDigest included) is identical from the story worktree and from the main checkout

adversarial.desc: The helper derives the state directory from core/brand-paths.ts; a fixture greps the helper for the retired literal state-dir spelling and asserts zero hits.

verification.selector: [PASS] structural: core/story-workspace.ts contains no state-dir literal (retired or canonical) and takes its paths from StoryStore

verificationEvidence.note: core/story-workspace.ts exports resolveStoryWorkspace returning gitCwd (via resolveGitCwd), a workspace-rooted store, workspace config and source; the structural case reads the four files and asserts delegation plus removal of their own logic; the helper cases assert linked-worktree and invocation-root resolution.

items.title: Add a mechanical audit fixture that enumerates every resolveGitCwd call site in handlers and classifies each as workspace-rooted or ctx.root-reading
items.context: Match call expressions (resolveGitCwd({...})), not substrings -- a file-level grep on main returns thirty-one files including a comment-only mention in validate-channel.ts, which receives gitCwd threaded from review-preflight.ts as deps.gitCwd. For each real call site, classify whether the same handler reads the story index, checklist or validate.commands through ctx.store/ctx.root rather than the resolved workspace, and print the classified list. The fixture is registered in the canonical inventories and its output becomes the scope of the follow-up draft migrate-resolvegitcwd-callers-to-workspace; this story does NOT migrate the flagged callers beyond the four resolver implementations in the previous item. RED: the fixture must initially report a non-empty flagged list.
items.userSees: `npm run test:single-owner-extraction` ends `single-owner-extraction-smoke: PASS` and prints a block headed `resolveGitCwd call sites` listing every handler file with a real call and, for each, `workspace-rooted` or `reads ctx.root: <which of story|checklist|config>`; validate-channel.ts appears under `comment-only mentions`. The suite name is present in test:serial-reference, RESOURCE_POLICY and validate.commands.

happy.desc: The audit lists every handler with a real resolveGitCwd call expression and classifies each as workspace-rooted or ctx.root-reading, printing the classified list.

edge.desc: validate-channel.ts is classified as a comment-only mention and review-preflight.ts as a real caller; a temporary fixture file with an aliased import is detected as a caller.

adversarial.desc: The suite is registered in test:serial-reference, RESOURCE_POLICY and validate.commands, verified by a fixture reading the real files, and the audit initially reports a non-empty flagged list (RED) that the story does not attempt to empty.
